title: Writing Equations in Slope-Intercept Form
keywords: algebra 1 linear equations slope intercept graphing writing point slope two points
intro: Rearrange an equation so y is by itself and the equation reads y = mx + b.
examples:
Example: 2x + y = 7
Subtract 2x from both sides: y = -2x + 7.

practice.question: Rewrite x + y = 5 in slope-intercept form. (Use y=-x+5.)

title: Graphing in Slope-Intercept Form
keywords: algebra 1 linear equations slope intercept graphing writing point slope two points
intro: Identify the y-intercept and slope, then graph the line one step at a time.
notes: Start with y = mx + b. Plot b on the y-axis. Use m as rise over run to find a second point, then draw your line.
examples:
Example: y = 2x + 1
Start at (0, 1). Rise 2 and run 1 to (1, 3). Draw the line through both points.

practice.question: For y = 2x + 1, what is the y-intercept? (Enter a number.)
practice.hint: Look for b in y = mx + b.

practice.question: For y = -3x + 4, what is the slope?
practice.hint: The slope is the coefficient of x.

title: Point-Slope to Slope-Intercept Form
intro: Use a slope and a point, then distribute and isolate y.
notes: Start with y − y₁ = m(x − x₁). Substitute the slope and given point. Distribute, then isolate y.
examples:
Example: m = 2, point (1, 3)
y − 3 = 2(x − 1)
y − 3 = 2x − 2
y = 2x + 1

practice.question: Given m = 2 and point (1, 3), write the equation in slope-intercept form.
practice.hint: Substitute into point-slope form, then distribute.

title: Finding the y-Intercept from Two Points
intro: Calculate the slope from two points, then substitute to solve for b.
notes: Find m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁). Substitute m and either point into y = mx + b. Solve for b.

practice.question: The line passes through (1, 3) and (3, 7). What is b?
practice.hint: First find the slope, then use y = mx + b.
